Vishvakarma.note: The architect of the devas, who built Lanka for Kubera and the chariots and weapons of heaven; son of the Vasu Vastu and Angirasi. His son Nala inherited the craft, which is how a bridge of floating stone reached across the sea. SB 6.6.13; Rama 6.22

Agni.note: The deva of fire, who carries the offering; one of the eight Vasus, sons of Dharma and Daksha's daughter Vasu. Father of the vanara Nila, whose effulgence the epic says was his father's. SB 6.6.10; Rama 1.17

BhanuDharma.name: Bhanu
BhanuDharma.note: One of ten daughters Daksha gave to Dharma (Yamaraja); her son Deva-rishabha fathered Indrasena. Not Bhanu, Krishna's son by Satyabhama. SB 6.6.2, 4-5

Lamba.note: Wife of Dharma; her son Vidyota generated every cloud in the sky. SB 6.6.4, 6

Kakud.note: Wife of Dharma; her son Sankata fathered Kikata. SB 6.6.4, 7

YamiDharma.name: Yami
YamiDharma.note: Wife of Dharma, one of Daksha's ten daughters given to him -- not Yami, Surya's own daughter and Yama's twin sister, the river Yamuna, already in this tree by a wholly different mother. Her son Svarga presides over the heaven that bears his name. SB 6.6.4, 7

Vishva.note: Wife of Dharma; mother of the Vishvadevas, the class of gods named for her. SB 6.6.4, 8

Sadhya.note: Wife of Dharma; mother of the Sadhyas, the class of gods named for her, old enough that the Rigveda already speaks of them as the gods before the gods. SB 6.6.4, 8

Marutvati.note: Wife of Dharma; her sons Marutvan and Jayanta are named for the storm-gods and for victory. Not the Jayanta already in this tree as Indra's own son. SB 6.6.4, 9

VasuDharma.name: Vasu
VasuDharma.note: Wife of Dharma, and the most consequential of Daksha's sixty daughters: her eight sons are the Vasus -- Drona, Prana, Dhruva, Arka, Agni, Dosha, Vastu and Vibhavasu in the Bhagavata's own naming (SB 6.6.10-11). The Mahabharata gives the same eight gods a different name each when they are born a second time, cursed, as Ganga's sons -- Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Aha, Anila, Anala, Pratyusha and Bhishma, already in this tree at Kurukshetra's era -- and only Dhruva's name survives both tellings. Not Vasu, Jamadagni's son. SB 6.6.4, 10-11

Muhurta.note: Wife of Dharma; mother of the Mauhurtikas, the minor gods who preside over the day's auspicious moments. SB 6.6.4, 9

Sankalpa.note: Wife of Dharma; her son, also named Sankalpa, is will and intention itself made a person. SB 6.6.4, 9

Patangi.note: One of Kashyapa's seventeen wives, a daughter of Daksha; mother of every bird. SB 6.6.2, 21-22

Yamini.note: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the locusts. SB 6.6.21-22

Kashtha.note: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of every hoofed animal whose hoof does not split, the horse foremost among them. SB 6.6.29-31

SaramaKashyap.name: Sarama
SaramaKashyap.note: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the tigers, lions and other predatory beasts. Not Sarama the rakshasi who comforted Sita in captivity, already in this tree as Vibhishana's wife. SB 6.6.24-26

Timi.note: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of every creature that lives in water. SB 6.6.24-26

Svadha.note: Wife of Angiras, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the Pitrs, the ancestors to whom every shraddha offering is made. SB 6.6.2, 19

SatiAngirasa.name: Sati
SatiAngirasa.note: Wife of Angiras, a daughter of Daksha, and mother by him of the Atharvangirasa -- the fourth Veda, in verse form. Not the Sati of the Shiva story, another daughter of Daksha who shares only the name: a different wife, a different husband, and not in this tree, by the same decision that leaves Shiva out of it. SB 6.6.2, 19

ArcisKrishashva.name: Archis
ArcisKrishashva.note: Wife of the sage Krishashva, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the comet Dhumaketu. Not Archi, wife of Prithu -- a different woman the same word, arci ('flame'), also names. SB 6.6.2, 20

Dhishana.note: Wife of the sage Krishashva, a daughter of Daksha; mother of four sons -- Vedashira, Devala, Vayuna and Manu. Krishashva's first wife, Archis, mothered Dhumaketu alone; the text (SB 6.6.20) attributes each set of children to one wife, not both. SB 6.6.2, 20

DevaRishabha.name: Deva-rishabha
DevaRishabha.note: Son of Bhanu and Dharma; father of Indrasena. SB 6.6.5

people.Vidyota: Son of Lamba and Dharma; generated every cloud in the sky. SB 6.6.6
people.Sankata: Son of Kakud and Dharma; father of Kikata. SB 6.6.6
people.Svarga: Son of Yami and Dharma; presides over the heaven that bears his name. SB 6.6.6
people.Arthasiddhi: Son of Sadhya and Dharma, named among the Sadhyas; the rest of that class is left ungrouped, as Vishvadevas is for Vishva. SB 6.6.7
people.Marutvan: Son of Marutvati and Dharma, named for the storm-gods; the Bhagavata calls him and his brother Jayanta expansions of Vasudeva himself. SB 6.6.9

JayantaMarutvati.name: Jayanta
JayantaMarutvati.note: Son of Marutvati and Dharma, named for victory; the Bhagavata calls him and his brother Marutvan expansions of Vasudeva himself. Not the Jayanta already in this tree as Indra's own son. SB 6.6.9

SankalpaS.name: Sankalpa
SankalpaS.note: Son of Sankalpa and Dharma, sharing his mother's name: will and intention itself made a person twice over. SB 6.6.9

people.Indrasena: Son of Deva-rishabha, in Bhanu's line from Dharma. SB 6.6.5
people.Kikata: Son of Sankata, in Kakud's line from Dharma; his own descendants are called the Durgas, guardians of fortresses (durga is the word for fort) -- a class left ungrouped rather than named individually, and no relation to the goddess who shares the word. SB 6.6.6
people.Nandi: Son of Svarga, in Yami's line from Dharma. Not Nandi, Shiva's bull and gatekeeper -- an unrelated figure sharing only the name. SB 6.6.6
people.Dhumaketu: Son of Krishashva and Archis; the comet, an ill omen given a father and a name of his own. SB 6.6.20
people.Vedashira: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana. SB 6.6.20
people.Devala: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana. Not the sage Devala of the Mahabharata, a much later figure sharing only the name. SB 6.6.20
people.Vayuna: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana. SB 6.6.20

ManuKrishashva.name: Manu
ManuKrishashva.note: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana, sharing a common name ('the thinking one') rather than any connection to Svayambhuva or Vaivasvata Manu, both already in this tree. SB 6.6.20

Vastu.note: One of the eight Vasus, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vasu. By his wife Angirasi he fathered Vishvakarma, the architect of the devas — which is the parentage this tree needed, since the other account makes Vishvakarma a son of the Vasu Prabhasa, and Prabhasa in this tree is Bhishma. SB 6.6.10-13

Angirasi.note: Of the Angirasa house; wife of the Vasu Vastu and mother of Vishvakarma. SB 6.6.13

vdVasu.name: Vasu
vdVasu.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — wealth. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdSatya.name: Satya
vdSatya.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — truth. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdKratu.name: Kratu
vdKratu.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — the will that carries a sacrifice through. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdDaksha.name: Daksha
vdDaksha.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — skill. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdKala.name: Kala
vdKala.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — time. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdKama.name: Kama
vdKama.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — desire. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdDhriti.name: Dhriti
vdDhriti.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — steadiness. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdKuru.name: Kuru
vdKuru.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — the doer. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdPururavas.name: Pururavas
vdPururavas.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — the far-crying. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

vdMadravas.name: Madravas
vdMadravas.note: One of the Vishvadevas, the all-gods, sons of Dharma by Daksha's daughter Vishva — the glad-sounding. They are the deities a shraddha offering goes to when no other is named, which is why every ancestor rite in this tree passes through them. SB 6.6.9; the ten names from the Vayu and Matsya lists.

unions.note: SB 6.6.9 names Vishva's sons the Vishvadevas without listing them; the ten names are the Vayu and Matsya lists, which agree with each other. Several are names this tree already uses for other people — Kratu, Daksha, Kala, Kuru, Pururavas — and none of them is that person.

SB 6.6.10 gives Vasu eight sons, the eight Vasus: Drona, Prana, Dhruva, Arka, Agni, Dosha, Vastu and Vibhavasu. Only two are drawn here, because the other six are already in this tree at row 88 as the sons Ganga bore Shantanu and drowned — the same eight in a later birth, cursed down for stealing Vasishtha's cow, seven released at once and the eighth left to live it out as Bhishma. Drawing them twice would say there were sixteen. What the two here are for is that both were islands: Agni is one of the eight, and Vastu is Vishvakarma's father.
